summary: Provisioning fails when hidden SSID and device certificate rotation coincide during post-repair check-in
description:
Issue summary: Several recently repaired laptops fail final check-in during depot handoff when configured to connect to a company hidden SSID. Failure window correlates with scheduled device certificate rotation. Impact: Devices do not complete autopilot/intune post-provisioning tasks and are left in 'Pending enrollment' state; engineers and depot team must manually complete steps. Environment: prod us-west, affected fleet subset processed by Depot A between 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-09.

Observed behavior: During network configuration step the provisioning-agent repeatedly fails to establish WPA2-Enterprise session to the hidden SSID. NetworkManager logs show EAP TLS handshake failure with TLS alert "unknown_ca" immediately after certificate rotation window begins. Devices with visible SSID or those using cached certs succeed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Image device with standard corporate image and apply latest security baseline (2026-03-05 image).
2) Configure wireless profile for hidden SSID corp_hidden_eap with user/device cert auth (EAP-TLS) during OOBE/autopilot flow.
3) Trigger client certificate rotation from internal CA (scheduled rotation job).
4) Allow device to attempt network connection and post-provisioning check-in.

Expected: Device completes EAP-TLS handshake using new cert chain and finishes Intune/Autopilot tasks.
Observed: NetworkManager/EAP TLS fails with unknown_ca and provisioning stalls at post-provisioning checks.
logs: Mar 09 08:14:22 deviceX NetworkManager[1123]: <info>  [wlan0]: attempting EAP-TLS with identity 'device-cert'
Mar 09 08:14:22 deviceX wpa_supplicant[1200]: TLS: Certificate chain verification failed: error=20 (unable to get local issuer certificate)
Mar 09 08:14:22 deviceX provisioning-agent[2045]: ERROR: device-checkin: network-auth-failed (unknown_ca)
Mar 09 08:14:23 deviceX intune-agent[3099]: WARN: Enrollment stalled: awaiting network connectivity
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: CA rotation produced a short period where devices had either old cert chain cached or the CA bundle change wasn't propagated to local trust store before new device cert issuance. Depot network uses RADIUS with TLS client validation; RADIUS server logs show successful acceptance for some devices and immediate reject for others with 'client cert chain invalid'. We reproduced locally by forcing CA chain swap on RADIUS while a device requested a new cert: the device validated server cert against cached intermediates and rejected new chain. Another contributing factor: NetworkManager does a cert chain validation before using freshly provisioned device cert if the local NSS/Trust store is out-of-sync.

We verified: 1) Devices with prior cached chain succeed. 2) Devices that obtain device cert after CA rotation often fail until NSS cache is reloaded or a reboot occurs. 3) Workstations using visible SSID fall back to cached WPA credentials and complete post-provisioning, so issue is specific to EAP-TLS timing and hidden SSID behavior.

Correlated logs and depot schedule indicate a rotation job ran 2026-03-08 23:30 UTC affecting our CA and intermediate bundles on Enrollment CA.
comments: Samira Patel (Support) 2026-03-09: Report received from Depot A — 8 devices failed final check-in with same error. Escalating to Networking + Identity team.

Diego Martinez (Assigned) 2026-03-09: Reproduced locally with test bench. Confirmed unknown_ca in wpa_supplicant. Opening request with Identity team to confirm CA rotation windows and overlap behavior.

Riley Chen (Identity) 2026-03-10: Identity team confirms automated CA swap completed 2026-03-08 23:30 UTC. We allowed new intermediates to be published but did not push NSS trust cache update to depot imaging nodes. We'll prepare a revocation/roll-forward note and advise on mitigation.

Diego Martinez (Networking) 2026-03-10: Quick mitigation: temporarily enable 'visible SSID' profile fallback for depot VLAN and perform forced NSS cache reload after device cert issuance. Scheduling script to trigger 'update-ca-trust' and service restart on imaging fleet during next rotation window.

Samira Patel (Support) 2026-03-11: Depot team confirmed scripted NSS cache update allowed 6/8 stuck devices to proceed without full manual intervention. Two devices required manual reboot and re-enroll.
current_workaround: 1) Update depot imaging nodes to push new CA bundle and trigger NSS/OpenSSL cache refresh immediately after CA rotation. 2) Temporarily enable a visible SSID network profile for depot VLAN to allow devices to complete enrollment and then re-apply hidden SSID on completion. 3) For already stuck devices, reboot and run 'update-ca-trust' + restart NetworkManager.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied on 2026-03-11: deployed CA bundle push job to depot imaging fleet and added a post-rotation hook to refresh trust stores and restart NetworkManager/sssd where applicable. Two affected devices required manual re-enroll; logged serials and completed by depot technicians. Identity team to add transparent CA rotation playbook to Confluence and notify Depot lead before future rotations.
next_steps: 1) Identity: implement zero-downtime CA rotation playbook that includes trust-bundle push to imaging/depot nodes and a post-rotation verification step.
2) Provisioning: add pre-rotation guardrail to avoid scheduling large depot handoffs during known rotation windows.
3) Networking: add ephemeral visible-SSID fallback as an automatable mitigation during depot flows.
4) Ops: run one simulated CA rotation in staging with imaging fleet to validate hooks (target date 2026-03-18).
